notebook_contract: 01 basic breakdown: repeat the standard descriptive, missingness, cardinality and train/test coverage checks for the feature type.
02 noteworthy findings: identify supported target relationships, interpret the single-feature evidence and record a provisional decision.
03 related features: name the relationships worth checking, quantify them with a type-appropriate diagnostic and explain the modelling consequence.

features.name: amount_tsh
features.disposition: retain with availability and positive-magnitude treatment
features.finding: Zero dominates the supplied values and positive amounts are strongly right-skewed.
features.decision: Keep an amount-recorded indicator and compare raw or transformed positive magnitude inside validation.
features.risk: Zero can mean no recorded amount rather than a genuine measured zero.

related.reason: Payment arrangement provides the closest semantic context for a recorded tariff amount.
Water availability may influence whether an amount is charged or recorded.

features.name: date_recorded
features.disposition: derive recording year and month
features.finding: Every supplied date parses, but collection timing is concentrated in survey waves.
features.decision: Derive stable calendar components and avoid one-hot encoding every raw date.
features.risk: Recording time can proxy survey operations and geography rather than waterpoint condition.

related.reason: Together they define waterpoint age at observation.
Survey waves may have moved through regions at different times.
Installer activity and recorded construction cohorts may be time-dependent.

features.name: funder
features.disposition: retain after conservative normalisation and fold-fitted rare grouping
features.finding: Effective missingness is about 7.5% and a small but material test share uses unseen funders.
features.decision: Keep blank and sentinel states distinct, normalise conservatively and handle unseen levels explicitly.
features.risk: Naive target encoding leaks and unrestricted fuzzy merging can combine different organisations.

related.reason: Funding and installation organisations are strongly associated but not duplicates.
A funder may repeatedly support named schemes.
Organisation activity is geographically concentrated.

features.name: gps_height
features.disposition: retain zero availability and measured elevation separately
features.finding: Zero affects roughly a third of rows and overlaps a broader missing-measurement block.
features.decision: Flag zero, impute it inside folds where necessary and preserve negative measured values initially.
features.risk: Some zeros can be genuine low elevation and the feature is geographically structured.

related.reason: Elevation is spatially structured and coordinate missingness overlaps height zero.
Elevation is spatially structured and coordinate missingness overlaps height zero.
Height and population zeros frequently occur in the same measurement block.
Height and construction-year zeros frequently co-occur.

features.name: installer
features.disposition: retain after conservative normalisation and fold-fitted rare grouping
features.finding: The field contains case and whitespace fragmentation as well as blank and sentinel values.
features.decision: Normalise case and whitespace, retain separately from funder and map unseen values explicitly.
features.risk: Aliases need a reviewed mapping; fuzzy merging can erase meaningful distinctions.

related.reason: Funding and installation organisations are strongly related but not equivalent.
Installers operate in particular construction cohorts.
Installers can be associated with repeated named schemes.

features.name: longitude
features.disposition: retain only as part of a validated coordinate pair
features.finding: Longitude zero participates in the paired missing-location sentinel.
features.decision: Create one coordinate-availability flag and transform longitude and latitude together.
features.risk: Using either coordinate independently breaks location meaning and encourages spatial memorisation.

related.reason: The two values are one inseparable geographic coordinate.
Named region should broadly agree with coordinate location.
Administrative geography gives a categorical back-off for location.
Coordinate and height missingness overlap and both describe physical location.

features.name: latitude
features.disposition: retain only as part of a validated coordinate pair
features.finding: Latitude near zero participates in the paired missing-location sentinel.
features.decision: Create one coordinate-availability flag and transform latitude and longitude together.
features.risk: Using either coordinate independently breaks location meaning and encourages spatial memorisation.

related.reason: The two values are one inseparable geographic coordinate.
Named region should broadly agree with coordinate location.
Administrative geography gives a categorical back-off for location.
Coordinate and height missingness overlap and both describe physical location.

features.name: wpt_name
features.disposition: exclude raw exact value from the first baseline
features.finding: Most levels are sparse and more than half of test rows use unseen exact names.
features.decision: Exclude raw one-hot names initially; test cross-fitted frequency or text features separately.
features.risk: In-sample lookup performance is dominated by memorisation and geographic proxying.

related.reason: Waterpoint names may repeat within local settlements.
Administrative context can disambiguate generic waterpoint names.
Waterpoint and scheme names may share project identity.

features.name: num_private
features.disposition: retain only as an ablation candidate
features.finding: The undocumented field is almost entirely zero with a small number of extreme positive values.
features.decision: Keep a non-zero flag and magnitude candidate, then test an early omission ablation.
features.risk: Zero has no documented missing-value meaning and positive support is sparse.

related.reason: Both are numeric local-context fields and may share collection behaviour.
The undocumented count may relate to local participation or ownership.

features.name: basin
features.disposition: retain as stable low-cardinality geography
features.finding: Nine complete levels have stable train/test coverage and meaningful target differences.
features.decision: Retain as a categorical feature and compare its contribution with administrative geography.
features.risk: Hydrological and administrative geography overlap without forming a strict hierarchy.

related.reason: Hydrological basins cross administrative regions.
Water source types differ across hydrological basins.
Basin assignment is spatially structured.
Basin assignment is spatially structured.

features.name: subvillage
features.disposition: exclude raw one-hot value from the first baseline
features.finding: The field is extremely sparse, has reused names and exposes many test rows to unseen levels.
features.decision: Use only a separately validated hashing or frequency treatment with explicit missingness.
features.risk: Direct encoding encourages local memorisation and poor unseen coverage.

related.reason: Subvillages sit within wards, although names are reused.
LGA context partially disambiguates repeated subvillage names.
Waterpoint names can repeat within local settlements.
Region is the broad administrative back-off.

features.name: region
features.disposition: retain as interpretable geographic back-off
features.finding: All 21 levels are covered and functional rates differ substantially by region.
features.decision: Retain and add an LGA/region-grouped validation sensitivity check.
features.risk: Random validation can reward geographic memorisation.

related.reason: The named and coded fields overlap but are not simple duplicates.
Each LGA maps to one region in the supplied data.
Hydrological basins cross administrative regions.
Coordinates should broadly agree with named region.
Coordinates should broadly agree with named region.

features.name: region_code
features.disposition: cast to category and compare with named region
features.finding: The numeric-looking code has categorical meaning and is not a one-to-one copy of region.
features.decision: Treat as unordered and compare region, code and their combination by validation.
features.risk: Scaling or distance-based treatment would impose a false ordering.

related.reason: The code is an alternative but non-identical regional representation.
The pair forms a more useful administrative composite.
LGA mappings expose code reuse and anomalies.

features.name: district_code
features.disposition: cast to category and combine with region context
features.finding: The integer code is reused across regions and zero is not universally missing.
features.decision: Treat as categorical and prefer a region-code/district-code composite if retained.
features.risk: The same raw code does not identify one national district.

related.reason: Region context disambiguates the reused district label.
LGA gives a named administrative comparison.
Ward is the finer administrative level.

features.name: lga
features.disposition: retain with explicit unseen handling
features.finding: All 125 training levels are covered in test and each maps to one region.
features.decision: Retain and compare with the coarser region representation.
features.risk: Strong geographic target differences require grouped robustness checks.

related.reason: LGA maps deterministically to region in the supplied data.
LGA context disambiguates reused ward names.
Code relationships expose small administrative anomalies.
Named and coded district representations overlap.

features.name: ward
features.disposition: retain with LGA context and fold-fitted rare grouping
features.finding: Raw unseen exposure is small, but many ward names are reused and low-frequency.
features.decision: Prefer an LGA/ward composite or encoder with explicit rare and unseen handling.
features.risk: Raw ward names can be ambiguous outside their administrative context.

related.reason: LGA context disambiguates reused ward names.
Subvillages are the finer named location.
Region provides a broad back-off.
Coordinates provide an independent location representation.

features.name: population
features.disposition: retain zero, one and positive magnitude as distinct states
features.finding: Zero and one are large special spikes; positive values are strongly right-skewed.
features.decision: Keep zero and one flags plus a raw or log1p magnitude candidate.
features.risk: Zero is probably often missing while one may be a recorded placeholder or real small population.

related.reason: Population and height zeros frequently occur in one measurement block.
Population distribution varies geographically.
Local administrative context may explain population scale.

features.name: public_meeting
features.disposition: retain true, false and blank as distinct states
features.finding: About 5.6% of training values are blank and blanks differ from false.
features.decision: Encode three explicit states rather than mode-imputing blank to true.
features.risk: Missingness may reflect the survey process rather than pump condition.

related.reason: Both are nullable administrative booleans.
Meeting status may reflect the management arrangement.
Scheme governance may affect whether meetings occur.

features.name: recorded_by
features.disposition: remove before modelling
features.finding: Every supplied row contains the same recording organisation.
features.decision: Remove because a constant column cannot separate outcomes in this dataset.
features.risk: The removal assumption must be revalidated if a future source introduces another recorder.

related.reason: Recorder identity belongs to the data-collection process represented by recording date.

features.name: scheme_management
features.disposition: retain and ablate against management
features.finding: The field has source blanks and strongly overlaps management without being equivalent.
features.decision: Keep blank explicit and compare its incremental value with management.
features.risk: Parallel management fields may mostly add redundancy.

related.reason: Both describe management using overlapping labels.
Named schemes have imperfect management mappings.
This is the broader management concept.

features.name: scheme_name
features.disposition: exclude raw one-hot value from the first baseline
features.finding: Nearly half the source values are blank and the recorded names are high-cardinality and inconsistent with scheme management.
features.decision: Preserve blank and literal sentinels separately; test only fold-fitted high-cardinality treatments.
features.risk: Scheme identity can memorise projects and geography.

related.reason: Scheme names map imperfectly to the management label.
Management gives a complete lower-cardinality alternative.

Installers may repeatedly construct named schemes.

features.name: permit
features.disposition: retain true, false and blank as distinct states
features.finding: About 5.1% of training values are blank and blanks are independent of most public-meeting blanks.
features.decision: Encode three explicit states independently of public_meeting.
features.risk: Permit status may proxy administration and geography.

related.reason: Both are nullable administrative booleans.

Management arrangement may influence permitting.

features.name: construction_year
features.disposition: derive valid pump age and retain unknown-year state
features.finding: Year zero affects about a third of rows and a small number of derived ages are negative.
features.decision: Keep unknown and inconsistent flags plus valid pump age or construction cohort.
features.risk: Age is missing for many rows and is confounded with technology and geography.

related.reason: Together they define waterpoint age at observation.

features.name: extraction_type
features.disposition: retain as the granular extraction representation
features.finding: Eighteen levels map deterministically to two coarser hierarchy levels.
features.decision: Start with the granular type and compare a coarse alternative by ablation.
